evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted check only requires positive, differing manager PIDs and nonempty, differing invocation IDs. If the guest reboots between the manager-restart snapshots, the new boot can satisfy both differences, so an accidental guest reboot is misreported as an isolated manager restart. The existing boot_id_changed check covers only the planned reboot phase. Requiring equal, nonempty manager-snapshot boot IDs while retaining the PID and invocation-ID checks is a small correctness fix to the existing check, not a new requirement or architectural change.
